items.label: Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 3 through 17
items.notes: Any course from Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 3 through 17 may be substituted for Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 1.

items.label: Cluster 70A
items.notes: Cluster 70A may be substituted for Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 1.

items.label: Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 1 Alternatives
items.notes: Any course from Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 3 through 17 or Cluster 70A may be substituted for Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 1.

items.label: Additional Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
Area Requirement
items.notes: Three additional 100-level Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences courses are required from below, other than M187, 189-199. Students may opt for one of the suggested grouped courses below

requirement.label: Honors Program
requirement.notes: The honors program in geophysics is intended to provide exceptional students an opportunity for advanced research and study under the tutorial guidance of a faculty member. Complete a minimum of two terms (8 units) of Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences 198 leading to the preparation of a satisfactory honors thesis.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Programming with MATLAB
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 33A
nodes.description: (Same as Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering M20.) Lecture, two hours; discussion, two hours; laboratory, two hours; outside study, six hours. Fundamentals of computer programming taught in context of MATLAB computing environment. Basic data types and control structures. Input/output. Functions. Data visualization. MATLAB-based data structures. Development of efficient codes. Introduction to object-oriented programming. Examples and exercises from engineering, mathematics, and physical sciences. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Evolution of Cosmos and Life
nodes.prereq_text: Limited to first-year freshmen
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Course 70A is enforced Use of concept of evolution, as it applies to biological organisms, Earth, solar system, and universe itself, to introduce students to both life and physical sciences. Examination of evolution of universe, galaxy, solar system, and Earth. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Earth Science
groups: Preparation for the Major: Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours; field days. Elements of Earth science; study of Earth materials; nature and interpretation of geologic evidence; study of geologic processes; historical aspects of geology. Mandatory field trips introduce students to solving of geologic problems in field. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Astrobiology
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Origin, evolution, distribution, and future of life on Earth and in universe. Course material primarily from planetary and Earth sciences, paleontology and biology, astronomy, chemistry, and physics. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Environmental Geology of Los Angeles
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours; field trips. Geologic hazards and natural resources of greater Los Angeles region. Topics include Los Angeles geologic hazards such as earthquakes, landslides, and floods; Southern California oil fields; gold and gem mining in region; local beach processes; and Los Angeles water resource problems. Field trips to San Andreas fault, California aqueduct, active landslides, and historic gold mines. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Earthquakes and Volcanoes
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, one hour; one optional field day. Description of causes and effects of earthquakes and volcanoes. Introduction to tectonic plate motion, faults, wave propagation, volcano formation, types of volcanoes, and volcanic eruptions. Review of earthquake and volcano hazard, societal consequences. Analysis of hazard reduction through earthquake forecasting, earthquake-resistant design, and volcano monitoring. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Solar System and Planets
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Properties of sun, planets, asteroids, and comets. Astronomical observations relevant to understanding solar system and its origin. Dynamical problems, including examination of fallacious hypotheses. Meteoritic evidence regarding earliest history of solar system. Chemical models of solar nebula. Space exploration and its planning. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Exploring Mars, Red Planet
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. History and future of Mars exploration, origin of planet, surface materials, and atmosphere. History of climate. Questions regarding water and life. Scientific and practical issues in mission design. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Natural Disasters
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; one field day. Global urbanization together with historical demographic population shift to coastal areas, especially around Pacific Ocean’s Ring of Fire, are placing increasingly large parts of this planet’s human population at risk due to earthquakes, volcanos, and tsunamis. Global climate change combines with variety of geologic processes to create enhanced risks from catastrophic mass movements (e.g., landslides), hurricanes, floods, and fires. Exploration of physical processes behind natural disasters and discussion of how these natural events affect quality of human life. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Blue Planet: Introduction to Oceanography
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Not open for credit to students with credit for or currently enrolled in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology 25. General introduction to geological, physical, chemical, and biological processes and history of Earth’s global ocean system. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Major Events in History of Life
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Designed for nonmajors. History of life on Earth as revealed through fossil record. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Dinosaurs and Their Relatives
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours; one optional field trip. Designed for nonmajors. Exploration of biology, evolution, and extinction of dinosaurs and close relatives, in context of history of biosphere. Information from paleontology, biology, and geology. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Natural History of Southern California
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, three hours; five field weekends. Identification, distribution, diversity of native plants and communities; identification and interpretation of rocks, minerals, and geologic features and geologic history of physiographic regions of Southern California. Emphasis on field-based learning. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Mineralogy: Earth and Planetary Materials
groups: Preparation for the Major: Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, four hours. Principles of mineralogy. Mineral structure and bonding and crystal chemistry, with focus on materials of interest for Earth and planetary sciences and major rock-forming minerals. Laboratory study of relationship between mineral structure and properties, including hand sample identification, microscopy (optical and electron), X-ray diffraction, and spectroscopy techniques. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Geologic Maps
groups: Preparation for the Major: Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, three hours; five field days. Recommended: course 1 (or any course from 3 through 17, 20, or Clusters 70A). Planning, creation, and interpretation of geologic maps, including both practical and philosophical problems that arise. Topographic and geologic mapping in the field. Interpretation of published maps in laboratory. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Stratigraphic and Field Geology
nodes.prereq_text: course 61
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; laboratory, three hours; fieldwork, eight hours per week. Recommended: 112. Principles of stratigraphy; geologic mapping of selected area; preparation of geologic report. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Structural Geology
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, six hours. Recommended: course 61. Planar and linear structures at different scales in sedimentary, metamorphic, and igneous rocks. Faults and folds, their description, classification, and kinematic and dynamic analysis. Deformation, strength, fracture, and rheological properties of rocks. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Continental Drift and Plate Tectonics
nodes.prereq_text: course 1, or any course from 3 through 17, 20, or Clusters 70A
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; computer laboratory/discussion, one hour. Designed for juniors/seniors in physical sciences. Exploration of history and phenomenology of plate tectonics theory, with particular focus on obervables and kinematics. Evidence supporting plate tectonics theory (magnetic anomalies, seismicity, gravity). Tectonic, igneous, and metamorphic processes at plate boundaries. Focus on plate kinematics both past and present and learn how to compute and plot velocities. Exploration of plate dynamics including driving mechanism and convection. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Applied Geophysics
nodes.prereq_text: course M71 or Civil and Environmental Engineering M20; Mathematics 3A, 3B, and 3C, or 31A, 31B, and 32A; Physics 1A, 1B, 4AL, and 4BL, or 5A and 5B
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, three hours. Recommended: course M171. Methods and knowledge involved in investigation of near-surface geophysics. Covers gravity fields, wave equations, seismic ray theory, reflection and refraction, seismic interpretation, basic earthquake source theory, and introduction to magnetic fields and electrical resistivity. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Applied Geophysics
nodes.prereq_text: courses M71, 136A
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory/discussion, one hour. Preparation: knowledge of Python or MATLAB. Recommended: course M171. Principles and techniques of exploration for mineral deposits using natural and artificial electric and magnetic fields. Methods include self potential, resistivity, induced polarization, electromagnetics, magnetotellurics, magnetics. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Field Geophysics
nodes.prereq_text: courses M71, 136A
nodes.description: Lecture, two hours; fieldwork, three weekends. Recommended: course M171. Application of seismic, gravimetric, magnetic, electrical, and other geophysical methods to geologic and engineering problems. Practical aspects of geophysical exploration, including planning, data collection, data reduction, and interpretation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Remote Sensing for Earth Sciences
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours. Designed for juniors/seniors and graduate students. Remote sensing related to development of natural resources. Characteristics of electromagnetic spectrum and review of remote sensing devices. Applicability to land-use classification, soil survey, urban studies, vegetation classification; emphasis on geologic interpretation of imagery. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics of Earth
groups: The Major: Additional Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 33A, Physics 1A, 1B, and 1C (or 1AH, 1BH, and 1CH)
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Recommended: course 1 or 8. Crust-to-core tour of Earth and physics used to explore it. Isostasy, plate tectonics, mantle convection, and geodynamo as discovered with tools of elasticity, seismology, fluid mechanics, and thermodynamics. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Oceans and Atmospheres
groups: The Major: Additional Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Life Sciences 30A and 30B, or Mathematics 31A, 31B, and 32A; and Physics 1A, 1B, and 1C, or 1AH, 1BH, and 1CH, or 5A, 5B, and 5C
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Physics of Earth’s oceans and atmosphere; biogeochemical cycles, atmospheric radiation and climate, energetics and dynamics of oceanic and atmospheric circulation systems. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Planetary Physics
groups: The Major: Additional Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 31A, 31B, 32A, Physics 1A, 1B, and 1C (or 1AH, 1BH, and 1CH)
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Formation of solar nebula; origin of planets and their satellites; comets, asteroids, and meteorites; celestial mechanics and dynamics; physics of planetary interiors, surfaces, and atmospheres. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Honors Research in Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Limited to seniors
nodes.description: Tutorial, two hours. Individual research designed to broaden and deepen students’ knowledge of some phase of Earth, planetary, and space sciences. Development and completion of honors thesis or comprehensive research project under direct supervision of faculty mentor. May be repeated for maximum of 16 units. Individual contract required. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Seismology
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 31A, 31B, 32A, Physics 1A (or 1AH), 1B (or 1BH)
nodes.description: (Formerly numbered 122.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, two hours. Recommended: course M71, Mathematics 33B. Earth mantle and core. Elasticity, seismic wave equation, ray theory, travel time inversion, surface waves, free oscillations. Earthquakes and source theory. Concurrently scheduled with course C222. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Perils of Space: Introduction to Space Weather
groups: Preparation for the Major: EPS SCI 3–17
nodes.description: (Same as Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences M7.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Concepts of plasma physics. Dynamic sun, solar wind, and Earth’s magnetosphere and ionosphere. Space storms and substorms and their impacts on astronauts, spacecraft, and surface power and communication grids. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computing for Geoscientists
groups: Preparation for the Major: Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.description: (Same as Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences M71.) Lecture, four hours; laboratory, 90 minutes; outside computing study, six to 10 hours. Introduction to writing programs, visualization of geoscience data, and comparison with models. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Fluid Dynamics
nodes.description: (Same as Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences M120.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Recommended: Physics 32. Fluid statics and thermodynamics. Kinematics. Conservation laws and equations of fluid motion. Circulation theorems and vorticity dynamics. Rotating frame. Irrotational flow. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Plasmas in the Laboratory, Space, and Engineering
groups: The Major: Additional Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 1A, 1B, and 1C (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: (Same as Electrical and Computer Engineering M185 and Physics M122.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, eight hours. Senior-level introductory course on electrodynamics of charged particles and their collective behavior in plasmas in laboratory, near-Earth space, and astrophysical settings. Covers selected applications taken from fusion energy, space weather, materials processing, generation of coherent radiation, and particle accelerators. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Advanced Computing in Geosciences
nodes.prereq_text: course M71, Mathematics 3A, 3B, and 3C (or 31A and 31B)
nodes.description: (Formerly numbered 171.) (Same as Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences M171.) Lecture, four hours. Misfit modeling and quantitative comparisons of acquired data sets and theory. Forward modeling from fundamental equations. Examples, experiments, and exercises from disciplines within geosciences. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Mathematics for Life Scientists
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Preparation: three years of high school mathematics (to algebra II), some basic familiarity with computers. Mathematical modeling as tool for understanding dynamics of biological systems. Fundamental concepts of single-variable calculus and development of single- and multi-variable differential equation models of dynamical processes in ecology, physiology, and other subjects in which quantities change with time. Use of free computer program Sage for problem solving, plotting, and dynamical simulation in laboratory. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Mathematics for Life Scientists
nodes.prereq_text: course 30A
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; laboratory, two hours. Introduction to concept of matrices and linear transformations to equip students with some basic tools to understand dynamics of multivariable nonlinear systems. Examples from ecological, physiological, chemical, and other systems. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Precalculus
nodes.prereq_text: successful completion of Mathematics Diagnostic Test
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Preparation: three years of high school mathematics. Function concept. Linear and polynomial functions and their graphs, applications to optimization. Inverse, exponential, and logarithmic functions. Trigonometric functions. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Calculus for Life Sciences Students
nodes.prereq_text: successful completion of Mathematics Diagnostic Test (score of 48 or better) or course 1 with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Preparation: three and one half years of high school mathematics (including trigonometry). Not open for credit to students with credit in another calculus sequence. Modeling with functions, limits, and derivatives, decisions and optimization in biology, derivative rules and tools. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Calculus for Life Sciences Students
nodes.prereq_text: course 3A with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 31B. Applications of differentiation, integration, differential equations, linear models in biology, phase lines and classifying equilibrium values, bifurcations. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Ordinary Differential Equations with Linear Algebra for Life Sciences Students
nodes.prereq_text: course 3B with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Multivariable modeling, matrices and vectors, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, linear and nonlinear systems of differential equations, probabilistic applications of integration. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Differential and Integral Calculus
nodes.prereq_text: successful completion of Mathematics Diagnostic Test or course 1 with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Preparation: at least three and one half years of high school mathematics (including some coordinate geometry and trigonometry). Differential calculus and applications; introduction to integration. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Integration and Infinite Series
nodes.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Not open for credit to students with credit for course 3B. Transcendental functions; methods and applications of integration; sequences and series. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Calculus of Several Variables
nodes.prereq_text: course 31A with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to differential calculus of several variables, vector field theory. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Calculus of Several Variables
nodes.prereq_text: courses 31B and 32A, with grades of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to integral calculus of several variables, line and surface integrals. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra and Applications
nodes.prereq_text: course 3B or 31B or 32A with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Introduction to linear algebra: systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, linear independence, subspaces, bases and dimension, orthogonality, least-squares methods, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, matrix diagonalization, and symmetric matrices. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Differential Equations
nodes.prereq_text: course 31B with grade of C– or better
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Highly recommended: course 33A. First-order, linear differential equations; second-order, linear differential equations with constant coefficients; power series solutions; linear systems. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 31A, 31B; and (Mathematics 32A) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Motion, Newton laws, work, energy, linear and angular momentum, rotation, equilibrium, gravitation. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Mechanics (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 31A, 31B; and (Mathematics 32A) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Enriched preparation for upper-division physics courses. Same material as course 1A but in greater depth; recommended for Physics majors and other students desiring such coverage. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Oscillations, Waves, Electric and Magnetic Fields
nodes.prereq_text: course 1A, Mathematics 31B, 32A; and (Mathematics 32B) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Fluid mechanics, oscillation, mechanical waves, and sound. Electric charge, field and potential, capacitors, and dielectrics. Currents and resistance, direct-current circuits. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Oscillations, Waves, Electric and Magnetic Fields (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: course 1AH or 1A, Mathematics 31B, 32A; and (Mathematics 32B) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Enriched preparation for upper-division physics courses. Same material as course 1B but in greater depth; recommended for Physics majors and other students desiring such coverage. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Electrodynamics, Optics, and Special Relativity
nodes.prereq_text: course 1A, 1B, Mathematics 32A, 32B; and (Mathematics 33A) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Magnetic fields, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, and alternating current circuits. Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, light, geometrical optics, interference and diffraction. Special relativity. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Scientists and Engineers: Electrodynamics, Optics, and Special Relativity (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: courses 1AH or 1A, 1BH or 1B, Mathematics 32A, 32B; and (Mathematics 33A) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture/demonstration, four hours; discussion, one hour. Enriched preparation for upper-division physics courses. Same material as course 1C but in greater depth; recommended for Physics majors and other students desiring such coverage. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics Laboratory for Scientists and Engineers: Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: course 1A or 1AH; and (course 1B or 1BH) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Laboratory, four hours. Computerized measurements of uniform and accelerated motion, including oscillations. Analysis of data and comparison of results to predictions, including least-squares fitting. Conception, execution, and presentation of creative projects involving motion. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics Laboratory for Scientists and Engineers: Electricity and Magnetism
nodes.prereq_text: courses 1A or 1AH, 1B or 1BH; and (course 1C or 1CH) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Laboratory, four hours. Sound waves and electric circuits, taken by digital oscilloscopes and analyzed by Fourier transformation. Geometrical and physical optics. Conception, execution, and presentation of creative projects involving sound waves or electric circuits. Letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Life Sciences Majors: Mechanics and Energy
nodes.prereq_text: Life Sciences 30A, 30B, or Mathematics 3A, 3B, 3C (3C may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; laboratory, two hours. Statics and dynamics of forces, motion, energy, including thermal energy, with applications to biological and biochemical systems. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Life Sciences Majors: Thermodynamics, Fluids, Waves, Light, and Optics
nodes.prereq_text: course 5A
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; laboratory, two hours. Thermal properties of matter, free energy, fluids, ideal gas, diffusion, oscillations, waves, sounds, light, and optics, with applications to biological and biochemical systems. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Physics for Life Sciences Majors: Electricity, Magnetism, and Modern Physics
nodes.prereq_text: course 5A
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; laboratory, two hours. Electrostatics in vacuum and in water. Electricity, circuits, magnetism, quantum, atomic and nuclear physics, radioactivity, with applications to biological and biochemical systems. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Mathematical Methods
nodes.prereq_text: courses 1A, 1B, 1C (or 1AH, 1BH, 1CH), Mathematics 32A, 32B, 33A; and (Mathematics 33B) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Vectors and fields; operators and transformations; matrices, tensors, and differential forms; ordinary differential equations and integral theorems; Fourier transform. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Analytic Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: course 32; and (Mathematics 33B) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Newtonian mechanics and conservation laws, gravitational potentials, calculus of variations, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics, central force motion, linear and nonlinear oscillations. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Analytic Mechanics
nodes.prereq_text: course 105A
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Conserved quantities, collisions and scattering, special relativity, non-inertial reference frames, rigid bodies, coupled oscillators, and normal modes. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Electricity and Magnetism
nodes.prereq_text: course 32
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Electrostatics and magnetostatics. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Electricity and Magnetism
nodes.prereq_text: course 110A; and (course 105B) (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour. Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, potential and fields, radiation, Lorentz invariance. P/NP or letter grading.

nodes.title: Introduction to Plasmas in the Laboratory, Space, and Engineering
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 1A, 1B, and 1C (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: (Same as Earth, Planetary, and Space Sciences M156 and Electrical and Computer Engineering M185.) Lecture, three hours; discussion, one hour; outside study, eight hours. Senior-level introductory course on electrodynamics of charged particles and their collective behavior in plasmas in laboratory, near-Earth space, and astrophysical settings. Covers selected applications taken from fusion energy, space weather, materials processing, generation of coherent radiation, and particle accelerators. Letter grading.
